Subject: Follow-up: Model fit & evals - recommended models, regression notes, next steps

Hi Jordan - great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the evaluation and make sure model fit and quality are aligned with Acme's support summarization goals.

Recap (from the call)
- Use case: customer support ticket summarization + short-answer retrieval augmentation (multi-turn).
- Key constraints: preserve F1 on factual extraction, prioritize brevity and correct entity resolution, latency target < 200ms p50 for 1-2 concurrent requests.
- Success metrics we agreed on: ROUGE/L and a small human-reviewed sample for hallucination rate.

Recommended models to try (shortlist)
- redwood-2.0 (pinned stable baseline) - we recommend starting here for functional parity and to measure drift vs older runs.
- redwood-2.1 (latest patch) - has throughput/latency improvements; we observed a few edge-case quality diffs in internal evals (details below).
- llama-3-13b-8k-quant - good cost/quality tradeoff for longer context if you scale retrieval.

Attachments and links
- acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached) - canonical prompt set we used on the call for both automated evals and human review.
- acme_eval_results_redwood-2.0_vs_2.1.csv (attached) - quick diff summary from our sandbox run.
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeEvalData (contains eval harness + scripts).

Quality/regression note (important)
- In our internal comparison we saw a small but repeatable regression on a subset (~2.7% of prompts) related to entity truncation when moving from redwood-2.0 -> redwood-2.1. The change is likely tied to a tokenizer boundary optimization plus a kernel selection tweak that affects some long-prefix patterns.
- We believe this is fixable and can be mitigated via pinning or canarying while we adjust the tokenizer rules.

Proposed next steps
1) You: share a small prioritized set of 50-200 golden examples (if possible) - we can run them against the three model options and share a batch-level diff.
2) We: run a canary (5-10%) of redwood-2.1 vs pinned redwood-2.0 on your evals and report hallucination/regression metrics and logs.
3) Joint call: schedule a 30-min engineer-to-engineer sync (Marcus/Dev + your eng) to review diffs and decide on pin vs rollout.

Would Wednesday or Thursday this week work for a short sync? If you reply with the golden examples and an availability window I'll get the canary run queued.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132

Hi Jordan, looping in the engineering details so you have a clear runbook.

Short answer on rollback/pinning
- Yes - we support pinning to a model_version identifier at the API layer (model=redwood-2.0; model_version=hash-20260203). Rolling back from 2.1 -> 2.0 for your traffic is a config change and can be done within minutes; we also support route-based pinning per environment.

What caused the regression (high-level)
- The regression looks tied to two coordinated changes in 2.1: a tokenizer boundary normalization (intended to reduce token count in some prefixes) plus a kernel scheduling change that altered how KV caching is handled for long-prefix multi-turn sessions. Together these produce occasional entity truncation when the prompt contains specific nested bullet patterns (we have the failing examples in the attached CSV).

Recommendation (safe path)
1) Pin production to redwood-2.0 (model_version=hash-20260110) while we triage. This gives you deterministic behavior.
2) We'll run a canary: 5% traffic -> redwood-2.1 with enhanced logging and the eval harness (we already set up the eval job once you share golden examples).
3) If the canary passes your golden set and the automatic hallucination/regression thresholds, we can widen to 25% then 100% with an automated rollback policy on regression.

What we need from you
- The prioritized golden examples (100 is perfect).
- Any hard rejection rules (e.g., entity changes not allowed, hallucination threshold > 1.5%).

Internal links
- Canary/runbook doc: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/canary-rollouts (internal)
- Diff report (sandbox): https://app.redwood.ai/evals/ACME-042

I'll coordinate with Marcus on the canary metrics dashboard and make sure you get token-level cost/latency breakdowns.

Thanks,
